additionalDevelopmentNotes: A Rust broadcast test initially used a shared sequence rather than each recipient inbox sequence; fixed only the fixture, leaving production delivery validation strict.
No production request limits were raised; ongoing group authorization is coalesced across mesh links.
The earlier fixed all-answer/end-on-leave draft was changed following direct user feedback, not treated as a technical encryption restriction.
limitations: Three selected devices from exactly three private-chat accounts; no persistent community voice channels or SFU
Unanswered invitees may join later; rejoining the same call after leaving and changing chosen devices remain open
Rekey rebuilds peer links and may briefly interrupt audio; no physical-network seamlessness claim
General MLS chat membership/epoch changes still stop capture and require a new call
Native runs use one isolated Windows WebView2 process with three real accounts and synthetic audio, test autoplay and native fixture storage
TURN is loopback Docker; TCP refers to client-to-relay transport, not TURN-TLS, public UDP reachability or an all-TCP media path
Physical capture/permissions, independent networks, NAT/firewalls, macOS/Linux, external SFrame interoperability and security review remain open
JavaScript/WebCrypto key destruction is not guaranteed secure erasure; selected endpoints can record/disclose content
